title: AI-Math and Programming for Business Analytics
units_note: Catalog lists 2-4; pre-term intensive graded S/U, treated as required prep (not counted toward the 50 units).

offerings.format_notes: Compressed two-week intensive with daily class and lab sessions.

description: An intensive summer gateway course that builds math, statistics, and programming foundations for the MSBA in a Generative AI era. Students implement core concepts (mean, variance, A/B testing, clustering) from scratch in Python without external libraries, practice test-driven development, and learn to collaborate with AI tools on business problems.
prerequisites: Assigned DataCamp coursework, self-paced online math & stats bootcamp, recommended OpenIntro Statistics review (Ch. 1-5).
workload_basis: Compressed two-week format: daily sessions, skills test, programming cases, probability problem sets, written and oral final exam.
grading: Pass/fail (S/U) based on written and oral final exam; individual assignments and participation count significantly.
notes: All work individual; students must be able to explain every line of code in person; some assignments allow GenAI, some forbid it.

title: Business Analytics in Marketing, Finance, and Operations

offerings.format_notes: Three modules taught by three different professors, each 1/3 of the grade.

description: A three-module intensive course introducing analytics applications in marketing, finance, and operations, each taught by a different professor. Topics span customer value and advertising measurement, time value of money and portfolio concepts, and process analysis with capacity and inventory fundamentals.
skills: evaluating advertising effectiveness and causal claims
financial decision-making with NPV and TVM
workload_basis: Per-module assessments: quizzes and exercises (marketing), group homework plus take-home and oral exams (finance), homework plus written and oral exam (operations).
grading: Three module grades, each 1/3 of the total; marketing module curved; oral exams in finance and operations modules.
notes: Paper quizzes with no devices; oral exams in two modules; preparation before class essential.

title: Collecting and Analyzing Large Data

offerings.format_notes: 8am Tuesday meetings; several flipped classes.

description: An introduction to tools and frameworks for collecting and analyzing large datasets to drive strategic business decisions. Covers the full analytics project cycle — scoping, data collection (web scraping, APIs, experiments), exploratory analysis, predictive modeling, and presenting findings — with a team project consulting for a real organization.
skills: collecting data via scraping, APIs, and experiments
workload_basis: Midterm and final exams, individual assignments, team project for a real organization, participation, flipped-class pre-work.
grading: 35% final exam, 20% midterm, 20% team project, 10% assignments, 15% participation.
notes: Team project consults for an actual business; GenAI encouraged but students must explain all submitted code.

title: Business Analytics
description: A foundations course in business analytics focused on using data, statistical models, and quantitative methods to make decisions under uncertainty. Covers decision analysis, statistical inference, simulation, regression, and optimization with hands-on programming in R and Python, applied through six team case studies.
workload_basis: Seven homework assignments, six team case write-ups, participation, plus 3-hour midterm and final exams.
grading: 35% final exam, 25% midterm, 15% case write-ups, 10% homework, 15% participation.
notes: Six group case write-ups in study groups; open-book but strictly individual exams; peer evaluations factor into participation.

title: Customer Analytics
description: Core course on customer analytics (no syllabus PDF was available; summary based on the Rady program website). Typically covers analytics for customer acquisition, retention and churn, customer lifetime value, and targeting/response models.
workload_basis: Unknown — syllabus not available.
grading: Unknown — syllabus not available.
notes: Core per the Rady MSBA website; details limited because no syllabus was in the source folder.

title: Business Analytics Consulting and Solution Design

offerings.format_notes: Five sessions; attendance mandatory.

description: A case-based course on designing effective business analytics solutions, emphasizing that framing the problem correctly is the most critical part of any analytics project. Students learn to translate business needs into solvable analytical problems, avoid common data-science failure modes, and plan modeling, prescriptive analytics, and deployment.
topics: translating business needs into analytical problems
workload_basis: Four assignments (mostly 1-page reviews plus a group capstone presentation review), readings, no exams.
grading: Four assignments (75 pts) plus attendance (25 pts); no final exam.
notes: Unexcused absence costs half a letter grade; students review live capstone presentations in class.

title: Business Analytics Capstone
description: The MSBA capstone: teams solve a real business analytics problem for an external sponsor company, covering the full project cycle from scoping and a client-approved charter through data preparation, analysis, and final recommendations. Emphasis on project management, stakeholder communication, and professional delivery.
skills: presenting to technical and nontechnical audiences
prerequisites: Taken in the final quarter; applies techniques from the whole program (requires MGTA 451, 452, 453).
workload_basis: Explicitly ~12 hours/week: weekly client and advisor meetings, biweekly peer surveys, mid-term and final presentations with individual exams.
grading: 25% professionalism, 25% teamwork (peer surveys), 15% output quality, 15% communication, 20% individual understanding.
notes: External company sponsor; mandatory weekly client and faculty meetings; strict data handling rules.

title: Data-Driven Communications

offerings.format_notes: Five highly participatory lab sessions.

description: A highly participatory lab course on presenting data through clear, compelling storytelling. Students use actor-training techniques to strengthen delivery, vocal range, and audience connection, building weekly presentations that culminate in a final storytelling-with-data presentation.
workload_basis: Weekly readings, presentation prep, peer feedback and reflections, plus a final project presentation over five sessions.
grading: 40% engagement/participation/peer feedback, 60% individual and group assignments; no exams.
notes: Attendance essentially mandatory (participatory lab); AI-generated work explicitly prohibited.

title: Analyzing Unstructured Data (NLP & LLM Applications)

offerings.format_notes: Five sessions; taught by an industry data science VP.

description: An applied course on natural language processing and large language models for business. Briefly reviews classical NLP (preprocessing, embeddings) then moves into transformers, prompt engineering, RAG, LLM agents, and multimodal models, with one comprehensive group project building an AI-driven business application.
skills: applying NLP to business text data
prerequisites: Math and basic statistics, Python programming, basic supervised machine learning.
workload_basis: One comprehensive group project with midterm and final presentations, plus quizzes and labs; no exams.
grading: 30% attendance/quizzes/labs, 30% midterm project presentation, 40% final project presentation.
notes: Team project (3-4 students); strict attendance policy; heavy GenAI use expected and rewarded.

title: Supply Chain Analytics
description: Links supply chain theory with data analytics applications: mapping a company's supply chain, managing demand and supply-side uncertainty, and communicating improvement strategies. Spans classical methods (newsvendor, forecasting, inventory) through last-mile delivery, sustainability, and revenue management, with hands-on Python and Excel work.
workload_basis: Weekly quizzes, 5-7 homework assignments, group case write-up, group final project; no exams.
grading: 10% participation, 10% case write-up, 25% homework, 25% quizzes, 30% final project; no exams.
notes: Quizzes every class (lowest dropped); group case and group final project; AI tool use encouraged.

title: Business Intelligence Systems

offerings.format_notes: Weeks 6-10 (second half of quarter); Tableau-focused, no Snowflake.
Weeks 6-10; adds Snowflake cloud data warehousing alongside Tableau.

description: A hands-on, project-based course on turning high-volume data from disparate systems into actionable insights through interactive dashboards. The Fall section centers on Tableau and Tableau Prep; the Spring section adds the Snowflake Data Cloud for scalable storage, SQL/ELT, and data modeling. Culminates in a team dashboard project and presentation.
workload_basis: One multi-part team project (design doc, prep workflow, dashboards, presentation, final doc) plus quizzes over 5 weeks; no exams.
grading: Mostly project-based (presentation + deliverables ~85%), quizzes ~5-10%.
notes: Half-quarter course (weeks 6-10). Portfolio-ready team project; GenAI use expected but logic must be explainable.

title: Experiments for Business Analytics (Experiments in Firms)
description: Covers how businesses and policymakers use randomized experiments in pricing, marketing, employee incentives, and consumer behavior, incorporating behavioral economics into experimental interventions. Groups develop a business question, design a randomized experiment, run a pilot study, and present results.
workload_basis: Midterm (35%), two small individual assignments, milestone-based group pilot project with presentation.
grading: 15% participation, 10% individual assignments, 35% midterm, 40% group final project.
notes: Quarter-long teams of 2-4 with peer evaluation; strict no-AI policy for assignments and exams.

title: Managerial Judgment and Decision Making

offerings.format_notes: Thursday/Friday intensive blocks.
Six 4-hour Saturday morning sessions (8am-12pm) — good for students preferring a weekend/compressed schedule.

description: A two-part course on making better decisions and getting them implemented. Part one examines judgment under uncertainty (heuristics, biases, noise, group decisions, models vs. intuition, risk taking); part two covers building influence through coalitions, networks, and persuasion, ending with a personal action plan.
workload_basis: Heavy reading and case prep, frequent pre-class surveys/assignments, take-home midterm, open-format final project; no coding.
grading: 25% participation, 35% take-home midterm, 40% final project (Personal Action Plan).
notes: Discussion- and case-heavy with graded participation; two sections with identical content but different schedules; AI use allowed with disclosure.

title: Business Analytics Project Management

offerings.format_notes: Five sessions; pop-quiz every class.

description: Focuses on leading analytics projects: designing and planning work, coordinating dispersed teams, managing senior-management expectations, and managing risk. Covers stage-gate processes, critical path and PERT scheduling, resource allocation, real options, modularity, and agile development, anchored by a team case building a Python simulation of uncertain project durations.
skills: Monte Carlo simulation of project durations in Python
workload_basis: Pop-quiz every class, two individual quizzes, two-part team case with code and design doc, final exam worth 40%.
grading: 10% pop-quizzes, 30% team case (write-up + code), 40% final exam, 20% individual quizzes.
notes: Attendance effectively mandatory (missed class forfeits pop-quiz credit); team deliverable is a reusable Jupyter Monte-Carlo tool.

title: Fraud Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Fully online (no physical classroom); no exams.

description: Teaches building statistical and machine learning models to detect fraud: raw data analysis and cleaning, expert feature engineering, algorithm selection, and model evaluation. Real-world supervised and unsupervised problems include credit card transaction fraud, NY property tax anomalies, and application identity fraud.
topics: ML algorithms (trees, random forests, boosting, neural nets)
skills: end-to-end fraud detection pipelines in Python
cleaning and profiling large dirty datasets
prerequisites: Good background in math and statistics and working ability in Python.
workload_basis: Ten individual homework assignments with weekly deadlines, including three substantial report-based projects on real datasets.
grading: 10 homeworks (130 pts) plus participation (10 pts); curved (roughly half As).
notes: Taught online by an industry fraud-analytics practitioner; real datasets; no exams; curved grading.

title: SQL and ETL

offerings.format_notes: Mixed remote and in-person Saturday morning sessions; proctored skills test each class; advanced SQL through window functions and recursive CTEs; ETL case with Python + Snowflake.
Quiz-heavy format with proctored in-class quizzes; ETL case project.

description: Foundational course on working with data in relational databases using SQL and on building Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) workflows. Progresses from database concepts through complex querying (joins, subqueries, aggregations, CTEs, window functions) to ETL pipelines producing analysis-ready datasets, ending with an ETL case project.
skills: loading and transforming data in Snowflake
workload_basis: Proctored SQL quizzes/skills tests most sessions plus a group ETL project.
grading: Mostly proctored quizzes/tests (70-90%) plus ETL group project.
notes: Highly test-based grading; strong foundation for any data-engineering-leaning role.

title: Scalable Analytics
units_note: Catalog lists 2; weekly programming assignments make it feel bigger.
description: Performing analytics at scale on big data: computer systems and parallelism fundamentals, distributed processing with Hadoop and Spark, and cloud-based analytics on AWS. Hands-on weekly programming assignments in PySpark and Python, including machine learning with Spark MLlib, Amazon EMR, and SageMaker.
skills: building analytics models on big data
using cloud platforms for scalable analytics
prerequisites: Solid Python programming experience required (all assignments in PySpark/Python).
workload_basis: A programming assignment every week (80% of grade) plus four strict closed-book quizzes.
grading: 80% weekly programming assignments, 20% quizzes.
notes: Strictly individual assignments; closed-book quizzes with no AI/notes; strong signal for data engineering roles.

title: Pricing Analytics
description: A heavily quantitative, hands-on course treating pricing as the intersection of economics, strategy, and data science. Covers value pricing, demand estimation from surveys, experiments, and field data, price discrimination, bundling, and subscriptions, applied to real managerial data with a team pricing-strategy project for an actual product or business.
skills: estimating demand and setting optimal prices
prerequisites: Statistics and regression knowledge expected; no prior economics needed.
workload_basis: Five short homeworks, in-class midterm, and a substantial team project worth half the grade.
grading: 10% homework, 10% attendance/participation, 30% midterm, 50% team project.
notes: Team project (2-4 people) with week-10 presentations; human-in-the-loop AI use encouraged.

title: Special Topics: GenAI for Business

offerings.format_notes: Co-taught; includes guest lectures and optional Monday work sessions.

description: A practical course on leveraging Generative AI to create business value: when and how to integrate GenAI into business processes and decision-making. Centerpiece is a quarter-long group project building an 'AI-coworker' prototype that automates a real business process, supported by modules on prompt engineering, RAG, tool use/MCP, and agent systems.
topics: GenAI for data generation and analysis
workload_basis: Quarter-long group project with milestones, individual assignments, and weekly TODOs.
grading: 50% group project, 20% individual assignments, 30% participation.
notes: Attendance-sensitive (absent/late more than once lowers participation grade); peer evaluations required.

title: Special Topics: Healthcare Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Compressed 5-week course; missing more than 2 of 5 sessions results in an F.

description: A rigorous introduction to healthcare decision modeling centered on cost-effectiveness analysis for evaluating competing health interventions. Covers deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analysis and Markov cohort and microsimulation models of disease progression, applied to a project on type 2 diabetes medications.
prerequisites: MGTA 453 or knowledge of probability and statistics.
workload_basis: Two homework assignments and a group project over 5 weeks; no exams.
grading: 40% homework, 20% attendance/participation, 40% group project.
notes: Strict mandatory attendance; niche but valuable for healthcare-focused careers.

title: Special Topics: Marketing Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Taught by Head of Analytics at GBK Collective (ex-Bain); no exams.

description: Develops technical, statistical, and communication skills for analytically-based consumer insights. Five topics — experimentation/causal inference, preference measurement via maximum likelihood, conjoint-based pricing with Bayesian methods, segmentation via unsupervised learning, and driver analysis via supervised learning — implemented 'by hand' in code and published as blog posts on a student-built portfolio website.
skills: building a portfolio website with Quarto and Git
workload_basis: Five substantial coding problem sets (~18% each) submitted as website blog posts; no exams; collaboration allowed.
grading: Five assignments ~90%, engagement and website quality ~10%; no exams.
notes: You leave with a public portfolio website of your coursework — a real asset for job searches.

title: Special Topics: AI & Prescriptive Analytics

offerings.format_notes: Mandatory attendance: missing more than 3 classes results in an F.

description: An integrated introduction to AI and prescriptive analytics: first half covers deep learning (MLPs, CNNs, RNNs/LSTMs, transformers, NLP, LLMs) plus interpretability and bias; second half covers discrete-event simulation, mixed-integer programming, and dynamic programming for data-driven decisions. Hands-on Python labs apply methods to operations, finance, and healthcare.
workload_basis: Five homework assignments plus take-home midterm and final exam over 10 weeks, with mandatory attendance.
grading: 30% homework, 20% attendance/participation, 20% take-home midterm, 30% final exam.
notes: Bridges predictive AI and prescriptive optimization — rare combination in one course.
